findings.issue: The UI changes `regions` in place but only updates `dirty` on pointer-up and valid field input. Moving an existing ellipse updates its center during pointer-move, but pointer-up never sets `dirty` for that drag. Switching images or reloading therefore discards the move without the unsaved-changes prompt.
findings.fix: Track whether pointer-move changed a region and set `dirty=true` on pointer-up for moved-region drags.

findings.issue: Ellipse creation uses the drag midpoint and half-deltas, but does not normalize or clamp the ellipse to the image. A drag that starts or ends on an image edge can produce a region outside the image; the UI marks it valid and enables Save, which the server then rejects.
findings.fix: Clamp the ellipse center/radii to the image bounds before adding it, or reject the creation and show the existing bounds error.

findings.issue: When an upload writes the source successfully but preview creation/write or catalog save fails, the source file is left behind. Retrying the same upload then hits `EEXIST`; if no catalog entry exists, the endpoint cannot recover because duplicate reuse only checks catalog images.
findings.fix: Make new-image storage/catalog publication recoverable: on failure remove only files created by this request, or validate and reuse matching orphaned files on retry.

prompt: Review only these new project image-intake/editor changes. No execution or changes. Report concrete correctness/security/data-loss issues with file, line, reproduction reasoning and smallest fix. Do not invent cosmetic findings or demand new capabilities. Requirements: source PNG/JPG bytes kept unchanged, duplicate sources reused, catalog revision protects edits, writes use existing project idle/mutation guards and boundPath, fixed trusted browser JS only, manual ellipse surface rotation is explicitly preparation not production readiness. Inspect upload/save/load, selection coordinates, async operations and shape validation. A pending UI or final pipeline feature is a known limitation, not a bug. Return JSON {findings:[{file,line,severity,issue,fix}],limits:[]} and keep it short.
